target.title: Add shareable subscription usage cards
target.body:
## What this adds

CodexBar already makes subscription usage visible in the menu bar, but those stats are difficult to copy, screenshot, or share. This PR adds a native **Share Stats…** action that opens a polished, fixed-size usage card designed for social sharing.

- Shows every enabled/configured AI subscription in one 1200×630 card
- Differentiates providers with their existing CodexBar colors and distinct lanes
- Combines locally tracked 30-day token and estimated cost totals where priced history exists
- Shows plan utilization or a clear connected state when spend data is unavailable
- Provides **Copy Image**, **Copy Stats**, and **Save…** actions from a local preview window
- Exposes the same local preview from Settings → Menu → Sharing
- Keeps the export privacy-safe: no account identity, email, project path, prompt content, or network upload

The card uses explicit provenance language (`locally tracked`, `estimated`) so quota utilization and locally derived spend are not presented as the same kind of measurement.

## Why

Usage is increasingly part of how people compare and talk about AI tooling. A share surface turns CodexBar's existing multi-provider view into a useful artifact without adding an account system or hosted backend.

## Verification

- `swift build`
- `swift test --filter ShareStatsTests` — 3 tests pass
- `make check` — passes; only the repository's existing locale catalog warnings remain
- Built, ad-hoc signed, and launched the release app locally
- Generated and visually inspected a real four-provider card using current CodexBar data

`Scripts/package_app.sh` completed the main Release build but the optional widget extension step is blocked on this machine by an Xcode `IDESimulatorFoundation` / `DVTDownloads` plugin-version mismatch. A no-widget app bundle was packaged and launched successfully, so this is noted as a local toolchain limitation rather than hidden as a code failure.

## Scope

This PR intentionally contains only the share-card workflow. A unified Settings usage/spend dashboard will follow as a separate PR.

## Design sign-off

`VISION.md` classifies new features as requiring sign-off. This draft is intentionally requesting maintainer feedback on the product surface, export contents, and privacy/provenance language before it is marked ready for review.
